headline: 2025 GOTY Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is down to $33
summary: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, a Persona-style RPG, is praised for its original story and music. It's noted for being a shorter RPG compared to its inspirations, a unique positive. The game is currently on sale for $33.

headline: CMF hit the balance between cheap and good clip earbuds
summary: CMF's new clip earbuds offer a balance of affordability and quality. Clip earbuds inherently compromise sound for comfort and ambient awareness. CMF's design addresses common clip earbud limitations effectively.

headline: The MSI Claw EX is the most important PC handheld since Steam Deck — I still wouldn’t buy one
summary: The MSI Claw 8 EX AI Plus is hailed as the most powerful PC handheld since the Steam Deck. It features a next-gen Intel chip and improved MSI design. Despite its power, the reviewer states they still wouldn't purchase it.

headline: Hoto’s new cordless soldering iron heats up in three seconds
summary: Hoto introduces its new I-A06 Cordless Soldering Iron as part of its modular Snapbloq collection. The iron can reach over 200 degrees Celsius in just three seconds. It offers an adjustable temperature range from 100 to 450 degrees Celsius.

headline: Grand Theft Auto 2 – The Legacy Review
summary: Grand Theft Auto 2 features significant technical improvements over its predecessor. The gameplay experience is described as far better than the original. Its unique and unfamiliar setting was a one-time experiment the reviewer is glad isn't repeated.

headline: Project Revenant, a Unique Precision-Aiming 2D Sidescroller, Announces Public Playtest
summary: Mayfly is developing Project Revenant, a unique 2D sidescrolling action game for PC. The game requires precision mouse aiming to target enemies, eliminating 'spray-and-pray' tactics. A public playtest for Project Revenant has been announced.

headline: ICMYI: This Week in IGN Game Previews: Wolverine, Star Wars: Zero Company, and More!
summary: This article compiles IGN's game preview coverage from the past week. Previews include Marvel's Wolverine and Star Wars: Zero Company. Other featured games are Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave and Job Simulator: Human Relations.

headline: The Lord of the Rings: War in the North Dev Warned Warner Bros. Not to Go Up Against Skyrim Back in 2011
summary: A Lord of the Rings: War in the North developer strongly advised against competing with Skyrim in 2011. The developer's warnings to Warner Bros. were reportedly 'overruled'. This reveals behind-the-scenes strategic disagreements from over a decade ago.

headline: Temporary ban on sale of disposable BBQs over wildfire risk
summary: A temporary ban has been placed on the sale of disposable BBQs. The government warns of 'significant risk' from single-use grills. The ban is due to current drought and heatwave conditions increasing wildfire risk.

headline: Farage faces renewed watchdog probe after Clacton by-election victory
summary: Nigel Farage faces a renewed watchdog investigation following his Clacton by-election win. The probe concerns a £5 million gift he previously received. Farage's return as MP for Clacton has reignited the inquiry.

headline: Prisoners charged over attack on Sara Sharif's father
summary: Two prisoners, Steven Sansom and Adam Watson, have been charged. The charges relate to an attack on Sara Sharif's father, Urfan Sharif. They also face other charges concerning an incident at Belmarsh Prison.

headline: Eurovision proposes new rules to reduce political voting
summary: Eurovision organizers are proposing new rules to curb political voting. Politically motivated voting is described as 'persistent' and 'deeply worrying'. The aim is to enhance the contest's fairness and integrity.
